intro.sub:
In the original 1in8b.life, your birthplace is drawn by population weight.
This version hands the choice to you — pick a country, live from 0 to its average life expectancy.
Every life is shaped by real stats: infant mortality, GDP per capita, education, suicide, homicide...
intro.cta.hint: You can skip the settings and just press Be Born. With no country picked, it's drawn by population weight.

intro.about.text: The original 1in8b.life was made by Jin's Earth with Claude, on real public statistics. This version reimplements the spirit of the original, focusing on 172-country real life tables, cause-of-death distribution, birth certificate, and a shelf of past lives. All stored locally, no upload.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.p1: We do not collect personal information that identifies you.
privacy.p2: All data (past lives, family trees, memoirs) lives in your browser's localStorage. The one thing uploaded is the memorial hall: when a life ends, its game-generated record (name, birthplace, events, family; never your uploaded photo or anything you typed) is stored on our Azure server and made public automatically. The lives are fictional simulations and contain no personal data about you. You can delete any of them, or turn auto-publish off, under Keepsakes → Public memorial. A hash of your IP is kept to prevent abuse; the IP itself is not stored.
privacy.p3: You can wipe all records any time by clearing browser data.
privacy.p4: We use Azure Application Insights for anonymous usage statistics: page views, country/region, device type and anonymous game events such as starting or ending a life. It sets two anonymous cookies (ai_user, ai_session). Names, IP addresses and anything you write are not recorded. No ads. It does not load when your browser sends Do Not Track, and you can turn it off below.
privacy.p5: Source is open — fork, modify, self-host.

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.p1: This work simulates a possible life based on real statistics (life expectancy, infant mortality, GDP per capita, disease rates…).
terms.p2: Results are statistical simulations; they do not predict any individual's fate.
terms.p3: Educational mode (add ?edu=1 to URL) filters out war, disease, and violence — for classroom use only.
terms.p4: Death, suicide, etc. occur at their real-world rates. If you're in a low place, please reach out to someone you trust or a local helpline.
terms.p5: This is not medical, legal, or financial advice.
terms.helpline: If you are struggling: US 988 Lifeline, UK Samaritans 116 123, international findahelpline.com.

de.relocate.title: A job in another city
de.relocate.body: A friend offers you a job in another city. The pay is double what you make now.
de.relocate.fact: OECD: in 2024, migrants earned on average 1.4× more than people who stayed home, but saw family 60% less.
de.relocate.go.log: You moved for the new job.
de.health.title: Health check
de.health.body: Your checkup flags blood pressure and weight. Your doctor suggests lifestyle changes.
de.health.fact: WHO: 17 million people die from cardiovascular disease every year; 80% are linked to smoking, diet, inactivity.
de.health.quit.log: You started to change your habits.
de.inflation.title: Prices are surging
de.inflation.body: Inflation is 12% this year. Your cash and savings are losing value fast.
de.inflation.fact: In 2022, 92 central banks hiked rates; real purchasing power fell ~8% that year.
de.inflation.dollar: Convert excess to USD or gold
de.inflation.dollar.log: You moved savings into hard currency.
de.inflation.hold: Keep it in local bank savings
de.inflation.hold.log: You held the cash in local savings.
de.illness.title: Health warning
de.illness.body: A checkup finds an early-stage lesion. The doctor recommends 6 months of treatment.
de.illness.fact: WHO: 5-year survival is ~90% for early-stage cancer, ~30% when late.
de.illness.wait.log: You decided to wait and watch.
de.parents.title: Caring for aging parents
de.parents.body: One or both of your parents is becoming less mobile. They need daily help.
de.parents.fact: WHO: in low/middle-income countries 70% of elder care is unpaid family work, mostly by women.
de.parents.nurse: Place them in a nursing facility
de.parents.kin.log: You asked relatives to take turns.
de.divorce.title: Crossroads in your marriage
de.divorce.body: Friction with your partner is growing. The children feel it.
de.divorce.fact: OECD: 2023 divorce rates: KR 1.9‰, TW 2.0‰, US 2.4‰. Happiness recovers ~2 years after divorce.
de.divorce.stay.log: You chose to stay for the kids.
de.job.title: A career pivot?
de.job.body: Stable job, slow growth. A friend is recruiting you to a startup with upside.
de.job.fact: BLS: average new job tenure is ~12 months; after the 4th switch, median pay is 28% higher.
de.conscript.title: Military service
de.conscript.fact: Nordic countries phased out the draft in the 2010s. 24 Asian states still keep it.
de.conscript.lottery.go: You were drafted and went in.
de.lottery.title: An unexpected windfall
de.lottery.body: You won (or inherited) a sizable sum. What do you do with it?
de.lottery.fact: OECD: 70% of lottery winners spend half their winnings within 5 years.
de.lottery.share.log: You shared part with your family.
de.mental.title: When things feel heavy
de.mental.body: Lately you sleep badly and feel unmotivated. Someone suggests seeing a professional.
de.mental.fact: WHO: ~1 in 8 people has a mental health condition; early help recovers 2–3× faster.
de.mental.tough.log: You decided to push through alone.
de.home.title: Buy a home or keep renting?
de.home.body: Your lease is up and your agent emails: "rates are low, want to look?"
de.home.fact: OECD: home ownership ranges from 42% in Switzerland to 96% in Romania; OECD average is 68%.
de.home.buy: Take out a mortgage and buy
de.home.buy.log: You bought a home with a mortgage.
de.home.share.log: You bought a place with friends.
de.loan.title: A friend asks to borrow money
de.loan.body: An old friend (or relative) messages: "could you lend me a few thousand?"
de.loan.fact: Pew: 60% of Americans have lent money to family/friends; 25% never get it back.
de.loan.help_otherwise.log: You connected them with other options instead of lending.
de.sabbatical.title: Take a career break
de.sabbatical.body: You have been pushing hard for years and your body is protesting.
de.sabbatical.fact: OECD: countries like AU/NZ/SE offer ~6-month career break schemes; most returnees report better work performance.
de.inherit.title: A relative leaves a business
de.inherit.body: A parent or elder dies and leaves the family business plus some assets.
de.inherit.fact: OECD: family businesses make up ~70% of global GDP and 50% of jobs; only ~30% survive to the second generation.
de.inherit.keep.log: You took over the family business.
de.inherit.split.log: You and your siblings co-own it.
de.relative.title: A relative needs care
de.relative.body: A childless aunt (or uncle) is becoming less mobile and needs long-term care.
de.relative.fact: WHO: in low/middle-income countries 70% of elder care is unpaid family work, mostly by middle-aged women.
de.promotion.title: A promotion
de.promotion.body: Your employer wants to promote you, but it requires moving to another city.
de.promotion.fact: BLS: promoted workers earn 13% more on average in the first year; 40% decline for family reasons.
de.promotion.take.log: You took the promotion and moved.
de.promotion.negotiate.sub: Try to find a middle path
de.promotion.negotiate.ok: Deal reached: remote work with a raise.
de.promotion.negotiate.no: Negotiation failed; original terms or decline.
sm.weekend.title: How to spend this weekend?
sm.weekend.body: After days of high-pressure work, the weekend is finally here.
sm.weekend.family.log: You went home for a meal.
sm.pocket.title: The change in your drawer
sm.pocket.body: You have been collecting loose change in a drawer. It is starting to pile up.
sm.pocket.fact: Kids who get to decide for themselves how to spend small amounts tend to have stronger money habits as adults.
sm.pocket.save: Put it in a piggy bank
sm.pocket.gift: Buy a small gift for someone
sm.call.title: Call home
sm.call.body: You have not been in touch with family in months.
sm.call.fact: Studies show one long-distance call a week with parents measurably reduces loneliness and disability risk later in life.
sm.call.visit.log: You bought a ticket and went to see them.
sm.call.later.log: You did not call this time.
sm.reunion.title: Class reunion
sm.reunion.body: Old classmates are getting together and sent a photo. It has been years.
sm.reunion.fact: Research shows friendships that cross distance hold up better than hometown ones: moving is the biggest cause of lost friendships.
sm.reunion.skip.log: You did not go this time.
sm.cook.title: Cook tonight
sm.cook.body: There are ingredients in the fridge and you are tired of eating out.
sm.cook.fact: The OECD recommends at least 400 minutes of moderate exercise a week; cooking is usually the easiest one to make a habit of.
sm.volunteer.title: Volunteers wanted
sm.volunteer.body: The community centre has posted a notice recruiting a few hours a week.
sm.volunteer.fact: Do-Good Lab: volunteering produces a lasting happiness boost larger than a holiday, and far cheaper.
sm.walk.title: Go for a walk
sm.walk.body: The weather is fine and your knees still work.
sm.walk.fact: WHO: 150 minutes of moderate exercise a week cuts all-cause mortality risk by 27%; half of that can come from walking.
sm.walk.later.log: You did not go out today.
sm.phone.title: Time for a new phone
sm.phone.body: The battery barely lasts half a day and the screen is cracked.
sm.phone.fact: Smartphone users worldwide upgrade every 2.7 years on average, though that cycle is slowly lengthening.
sm.phone.keep.log: You decided to make it last another year.
